questions.stem: If you are in any doubt about whether a risk of collision exists, what does Rule 7 say?
options: Assume no risk until the other vessel comes within one mile
Wait for the other vessel to sound a signal
Deem that such risk exists
Call the coast guard before acting
questions.explanation: Rule 7 states that if there is any doubt, risk is deemed to exist. That keeps you on the safe side while you gather more information.

questions.stem: The compass bearing of an approaching vessel does not appreciably change over several minutes. What does this tell you under Rule 7?
options: Risk of collision is to be deemed to exist
The vessel will certainly pass clear
The vessel is moving away from you
The compass is probably faulty
questions.explanation: A steady bearing on an approaching vessel is the classic warning that you are on a converging course, and Rule 7 says risk is then deemed to exist. It is not a sign that she will pass clear.

questions.stem: You are approaching a tug with a very long tow at close range. The bearing to the tug is changing slowly but clearly. According to Rule 7, how should you treat the situation?
options: Relax, because any change in bearing means you will pass clear
Risk may still exist, since a bearing change does not remove the risk when approaching a tow or at close range
Ignore the tow and watch only the tug
Only use the radar and stop looking out the window
questions.explanation: Rule 7 says risk may sometimes exist even where the bearing changes appreciably, particularly when approaching a very large vessel or a tow, or approaching any vessel at close range. A long tow extends far behind the tug, so the tug's bearing alone is misleading.

questions.stem: In poor visibility your radar picks up one faint echo for a single sweep, and then it disappears. A crew member says, "That was just clutter, so we can carry on." Which Rule 7 principle is most relevant?
options: Assumptions should not be made on the basis of scanty information, especially scanty radar information
Radar returns should only be acted on if they are confirmed by sound signals
The vessel with the stronger echo is the give-way vessel
A single echo always indicates a vessel on a collision course
questions.explanation: Rule 7 warns against assuming from scanty information, particularly scanty radar information. A single faint echo should prompt continued observation, not a conclusion either way. The last option is also wrong because it makes the opposite assumption from equally little data.

questions.stem: Which description best matches the use of radar that Rule 7 asks for on a vessel with operational radar?
options: Keep the screen on the shortest range scale to see nearby targets clearly
Use radar only when visibility is restricted
Glance at the screen once per watch to confirm the lookout's report
Proper use, including long-range scanning for early warning and radar plotting or an equivalent systematic observation of detected objects
questions.explanation: Rule 7 calls for proper use of radar, which includes long-range scanning to give early warning and radar plotting or equivalent systematic observation. Using only the short range loses early warning, and occasional glances are not systematic observation. Rule 7 does not limit radar to restricted visibility.
